finding_title: Category 2 Individual — assessable income cap and minimum/maximum tax
name: Gibraltar
reason: The one shipped Gibraltar HNW row is titled "Category 2 / HNW"; this finding is the Category 2 substance for it. Not enough for high: what it verifies is the TAX treatment (GBP 118,000 assessable-income cap, GBP 37,000 min / GBP 42,380 max tax), while the criterion an applicant is actually screened on is net wealth, which the same file records as changed to GBP 5m in June 2026 and could not verify.

finding_title: HEPSS — assessable income cap and fixed tax liability
name: Gibraltar
reason: HEPSS is a separate income-tax status for high-earning employees, not a high-net-worth scheme, so it does not sit inside gibraltar-hnw-residence, and it is not the Residency Regulations 2026 employee permit already shipped as gibraltar-employment-residence-permit. Needs its own row. Only the GBP 160,000 cap and GBP 39,940 liability are verified; the finding states the minimum salary and accommodation requirements were NOT verified.

finding_title: Category 2 — immigration permission is discretionary under s.19(C)
name: Gibraltar
reason: Same corpus row. Materially useful — it establishes that Category 2 is a tax status and that residence for a non-EU national is a separate discretionary grant. FLAG BEFORE APPLYING: the quote sources that discretion to s.19(C) of the Immigration, Asylum and Refugee Act, and the already-shipped gibraltar-employment-residence-permit row records that Residency Regulations 2026 reg. 26 repealed ss. 18-34 and Part IV of that Act with effect from 14 July 2026. The guidance PDF was fetched on 30 July 2026 and may be describing a repealed power.

finding_title: Category 2 — June 2026 net wealth and fee reform
name: Gibraltar
reason: cannot_determine. The June 2026 net-wealth (GBP 2m to GBP 5m) and fee reform was read only as a summary; quote_original is deliberately empty and the amending Legal Notice was not identified. This is the single most decisive fact about the route and it is unverified.

finding_title: Category 2 / HEPSS statutory detail in the consolidated Rules
name: Gibraltar
reason: cannot_determine. Rule-level detail for both the Category 2 and HEPSS Rules is second-hand from a delegated pass that was not personally re-fetched; no quote recorded.

finding_title: High Value Residency — minimum annual tax contribution
name: Jersey
reason: Direct match: the shipped row is "High Value Resident / business residence pathways". The GBP 250,000 minimum tax contribution under Art. 135A is quoted on gov.je. Enough for high on the HVR limb, provided the row is narrowed to High Value Residency and the "business residence pathways" half of its current scope is either dropped or verified separately, and provided the row records that 2(1)(e) is a housing-and-work status, not immigration leave.

finding_title: High Value Residency — income and property thresholds
name: Jersey
reason: Same corpus row. Quotes the qualifying income (worldwide earnings well above GBP 1.25m, guaranteed 10 years) and the same page carries the property minimums (GBP 3.5m house / GBP 1.75m apartment). These are the route-defining thresholds.

finding_title: High Value Residency — tax rate bands
name: Jersey
reason: Same corpus row. Tax rate bands (20% to GBP 1.25m, 1% above) are the tax treatment, not the qualifying terms; corroborating rather than load-bearing. Also carries the warning not to use the grandfathered GBP 145,000 / GBP 170,000 figures.

finding_title: Business Migrant (Innovator) — investment funds
name: Isle of Man
reason: The single shipped row spans "Business Migrant / entrepreneur residence routes", which is in fact two visas with opposite outcomes: Innovator (3 years, extendable without limit, leads to settlement) and Start-up (2y4m, cannot extend, no settlement). One update cannot express both. This finding is the Innovator half; GBP 50,000 investment funds quoted. Not high yet — the settlement claim that justifies the route being in the atlas failed re-fetch (see next row).

finding_title: Business Migrant (Innovator) — settlement after three years
name: Isle of Man
reason: Innovator half of the same split. The settlement quote did NOT re-verify against the cited gov.im page on the fixed gate — the page appears to have changed since 30 July 2026. Re-quote before authoring; this is the fact that puts the route in scope at all.

finding_title: Business Migrant (Start-up) — no extension, no settlement
name: Isle of Man
reason: Start-up half of the same split. "You cannot extend this visa." is quoted, but the terms that would make a row (2y4m duration, 2-year cap, GBP 945 maintenance) exist only in prose on the page and are not in any quote.

finding_title: Worker Migrant five-year settlement and Long Residence settlement
name: Isle of Man
reason: cannot_determine. Worker Migrant 5-year settlement and Appendix Long Residence are entirely second-hand from a delegated pass; the Rules PDF was never fetched. No quote. Would be a new row if verified, not an edit to the business-migrant row.

finding_title: Investor Permit — statutory basis
name: Fiji
reason: Direct match to the shipped investor row. Verifies the statutory basis (s.9(2)(c) Immigration Act 2003) and the FITB/Foreign Investment Certificate gate. Cannot go high: the official page publishes NO minimum investment, no duration and no fees, and the finding expressly says the circulating FJD 250,000 / 500,000 figures are absent from it.

finding_title: Three-year Investor Permit under the Immigration Regulations
name: Fiji
reason: Same corpus row — the three-year permit tier, cited to Immigration Regulations 2007 reg. 39. Also records that the official page is internally inconsistent (titled "Seven (7) Years Investor Permit" while describing only the three-year permit). Still no monetary amount anywhere official.

finding_title: Seven-year Investor Permit — FJD 250,000 threshold
name: Fiji
reason: cannot_determine. The FJD 250,000 seven-year tier under reg. 41(2)-(3) was read from a third-party mirror, not from laws.gov.fj. The finding also flags that the figure may belong to the Investment Act 2021 registration regime rather than immigration law — two different thresholds routinely conflated.

finding_title: Residence on Assured Income Permit — Fiji's retirement route
name: Fiji
reason: Fiji has exactly one residence row in the corpus and it is the investor permit; the Residence on Assured Income Permit (Fiji retirement route, 45+) has no row. Needs a new one. Cannot be authored at high: NO minimum asset or income figure is published, the FJD 100,000 figure in circulation is unsupported, and the page states no duration, renewal terms or statutory basis.

finding_title: Rentista — USD 2,500 monthly income requirement (statute text)
name: Honduras
reason: The shipped row fuses rentista and pensionado under one min_income of USD 1,500 — and that is simply wrong for rentista, which art. 23 sets at USD 2,500/month. Two thresholds cannot live in one row. This finding is the rentista half: USD 2,500 quoted from La Gaceta No. 36,924 via the UNAH OMIH gazette scan.

finding_title: Pensionado — USD 1,500 monthly pension requirement (statute text)
name: Honduras
reason: Pensionado half of the same split: USD 1,500/month quoted from the same gazette (art. 24), with the additional condition that the pension must originate abroad — which rentista does not require. This is the figure the fused row currently carries, so the pensionado half keeps it.

finding_title: Inversionista — USD 50,000 minimum investment (statute text)
name: Honduras
reason: Honduras has no investment residence row at all. Art. 33 numeral 2 sets USD 50,000 minimum, quoted from the gazette. Authorable at high as an investment row.

finding_title: Acuerdo 374-2025 — discretionary residence at 50% of thresholds
name: Honduras
reason: Not a standalone route and should not become one. Acuerdo 374-2025 opens a discretionary art. 21(8) gateway at 50% of the rentista/pensionado/inversionista money, entirely at the SGJD's "analisis, valoracion y criterio exclusivo" and creating no acquired right. It belongs as a pathway or variant on the three rows above. Note also that the derived figures (USD 1,250 / USD 750 / USD 25,000) are arithmetic, not quotations, and must not be recorded as published thresholds.

finding_title: Rentista — official requirement sheet and fee
name: Honduras
reason: Rentista half again, from a second official domain (SGJD tramite sheet): USD 300 fee quoted, and the sheet independently restates the USD 2,500 monthly requirement. Corroboration on a second official domain is what lets the rentista half stand at high.

finding_title: Reglamento detail and Residente Inmigrado permanent residence
name: Honduras
reason: cannot_determine. The Reglamento articles and the Residente Inmigrado permanent-residence category (5 years continuous) are second-hand from a delegated pass; no quote. If verified this would be a NEW Honduran general_permanent_residence row, not an edit. inm.gob.hn was refusing connections throughout.

finding_title: Start-up entrepreneur permit — 2026 income requirement
name: Finland
reason: Maps to a row that is ALREADY high, so it does not touch the sweep. Apply it anyway as a correction: the shipped row records min_income EUR 1,210, which is the HIGHEST of three regional tiers; the quoted 2026 figure is "EUR 1,210 / 1,090 / 1,030 per month, depending on where you live", so the floor is EUR 1,030 and a single number misrepresents it.

finding_title: Permanent residence — pre-8-January-2026 qualifying period
name: Finland
reason: Finland has no general_permanent_residence row. But the verified quote is the SUPERSEDED rule: 4 years applies only to applications before 8 January 2026. The current requirement (6 years standard, 4 for high income or advanced degree, plus an A2-C1 Finnish/Swedish language test) is unverified, as is the amending act number and the high-income figure. A row must not be authored from this quote.

finding_title: Entrepreneur / self-employed permit — profitability test
name: Finland
reason: Finland's entrepreneur / self-employed permit is a distinct route from the start-up entrepreneur permit already shipped, and has no row. Only "Your business must be profitable." is quoted — no euro floor, no duration, no A/B permit type. The finding explicitly warns against borrowing the start-up tiers.

finding_title: Startup visa, company-owner and investment-agreement routes
name: Lithuania
reason: cannot_determine. Every Lithuanian figure in this row is second-hand from a delegated pass that read e-seimas; nothing was personally fetched, and migracija.lt is an Angular SPA that serves nothing to a plain fetch. The corpus already carries lithuania-business-activity-residence (medium) and lithuania-startup-visa (high), so this would be an update to those plus possible new rows — but not on this evidence.

finding_title: Residence permit categories and the 2024 digital nomad amendment
name: Kyrgyzstan
reason: cannot_determine, and the strongest row in the file: NOTHING was verified on any official Kyrgyz source, and the finding's own conclusion is that "Kyrgyzstan should carry no route rows" until one is found. That is a direct challenge to the shipped kyrgyzstan-investor-residence row, which should be re-examined rather than upgraded.

finding_title: Business Residence Permit — USD 50,000 and source of funds
name: Malawi
reason: Malawi has NO residence rows in the corpus. The Business Residence Permit needs one. Not high: the quote carries only the source-of-funds sentence, while the USD 50,000 minimum, the 5-year validity and the renewal window live in prose on the page, and the page cites no Immigration Act section or Regulations class number.

finding_title: Permanent Residence Permit — five years ordinary residence
name: Malawi
reason: Second missing Malawi row (general_permanent_residence). The five-year ordinary-residence rule IS in the quote. Held back from high because the source is a department page that cites no statutory section, and the same eligibility sentence sweeps in an "assured income" retirement gateway with no published threshold — the route boundaries are not clean enough to author at high.

finding_title: Investor Visa Category
name: Sri Lanka
reason: Sri Lanka has ONE shipped row, "Residence Visa - investment / business categories", whose vague scope silently stands for at least three distinct programmes. It must be split, not updated. This finding becomes the Investor Visa row: USD 100,000 = 5 years, USD 200,000 = 10 years, quoted from the official Immigration Department guideline PDF.

finding_title: Golden Paradise Residence Visa
name: Sri Lanka
reason: Second half of the same split. Golden Paradise is a separate named scheme with its own USD 200,000 GPFCA deposit, 10-year validity and a 50% withdrawal allowance after year one — quoted from the official brochure. Folding it into the Investor Visa row would fuse two different deposit regimes.

finding_title: Digital Nomad Visa (DNV)
name: Sri Lanka
reason: Different category entirely (digital_nomad); nothing in the corpus covers it. USD 2,000/month quoted from the official guideline. IMPORTANT: the finding carries a stale-figure flag in the opposite direction from usual — heavy secondary reporting claims USD 1,500 and 5 years from 15 January 2026, and that could NOT be verified officially. Author the official USD 2,000 / 1 year and record the flag.

finding_title: Resident Guest Scheme (RGS)
name: Sri Lanka
reason: Third half of the same split, and the reason the split matters most: the Resident Guest Scheme is closed to new entrants (extensions only) on the department's own page. Carrying it inside a generic active investment row asserts an intake that does not exist. Author as a closed/inactive row, so it leaves the active sweep entirely.

finding_title: My Dream Home Visa Programme
name: Sri Lanka
reason: retirement_pension category; no Sri Lankan row covers it. USD 15,000 fixed deposit quoted, plus USD 1,500/month remittance. Also closed to new entrants (extensions only), so it should be authored as a closed row and does not add to the active below-high count.

finding_title: Colombo Port City investor / residential property lessee visas
name: Sri Lanka
reason: cannot_determine. Colombo Port City visa categories are confirmed to exist on the official gov.lk domain, but no minimum investment, no lease value and no duration are published, and the implementing gazette regulation was not located. Threshold unknown, not absent.

finding_title: Temporary residence permit for founders / participants / beneficial owners
name: Ukraine
reason: Direct match to the shipped row. EUR 100,000 quoted on the State Migration Service site, with the two-year validity that distinguishes this category from the one-year default. Enough for high, provided the row also records the martial-law caveat and does not assert the unverified CMU Res. 141 restoration of standard procedures.

finding_title: Immigration permit for investors (permanent residence)
name: Ukraine
reason: A DIFFERENT route from the row above and must not be merged into it — USD not EUR, Law on Immigration No. 2491-III not the Foreigners Law, and the outcome is permanent residence, not a temporary permit. Quoted from the consolidated statute on zakon.rada.gov.ua. Note the quote only re-fetches from the /print view; the plain URL serves a portal shell. Open question worth recording on the row: whether any annual quota is actually allocated to the investment category.

finding_title: Immigration permit for highly qualified specialists and workers
name: Ukraine
reason: talent_skilled; Ukraine has no such row. The statutory category is quoted but is purely qualitative ("acute demand"), with no occupation list, no evidentiary standard, no quota figure and no confirmation the SMS is processing these under martial law. The finding's own confidence is medium and that is the right call.

name: Maldives
reason: cannot_determine, route_id null. Explicitly NOT RESEARCHED — delegated to a background agent that never reported. Carries a next-step plan only. Maldives has no residence row in the corpus and this does not create one.

reason: cannot_determine, route_id null. NOT RESEARCHED; superseded in any case by the Nicaragua rows in peru-nicaragua-residence.json.

name: Palau
reason: cannot_determine, route_id null. NOT RESEARCHED. The corpus carries palau-rns-digital-residency-id (medium); the finding's own expectation is that the RNS.ID confers no physical residence right, which if verified would argue for demoting or re-scoping that row rather than upgrading it.

name: Peru
reason: cannot_determine, route_id null. NOT RESEARCHED; superseded by the Peru rows in peru-nicaragua-residence.json.

name: Romania
reason: cannot_determine, route_id null. NOT RESEARCHED. Romania still has two below-high rows (romania-commercial-activity-long-stay, romania-digital-nomad-visa) and this addresses neither.

name: San Marino
reason: cannot_determine, route_id null. NOT RESEARCHED. san-marino-elective-residence remains below high and untouched.

name: Seychelles
reason: cannot_determine, route_id null. NOT RESEARCHED. seychelles-gopid-investor-residence remains below high and untouched.

finding_title: Calidad migratoria Inversionista (investor residence)
name: Peru
reason: Direct match. S/ 500,000 quoted from the Migraciones Ley y Reglamento PDF (Reglamento art. 86.1 lit. a), corroborated on the gob.pe tramite page. Enough for high. Record art. 86.1's own caveat that the amount may be changed by Resolucion de Superintendencia, and that the 2026 tramite page has dropped the numeral in favour of "el monto establecido en la normativa migratoria vigente".

finding_title: Calidad migratoria Rentista (pension / permanent passive income)
name: Peru
reason: Direct match, and the corpus already carries USD 1,000. Held back from high for a specific reason: the quote deliberately STOPS SHORT of the amount ("...ingreso neto permanente no menor a"), so the figure itself is not character-verified by any quote in this file — it lives in prose. The gate normalises whitespace, so the double space that motivated the truncation is not an obstacle; re-quote to include "US$ 1,000.00". Separately, the Reglamento (art. 92.2) leaves the amount to an acto administrativo of MIGRACIONES which the finding could not locate, so the figure rests on tramite pages rather than a numbered instrument.

finding_title: Calidad migratoria Permanente (permanent residence after 3 years)
name: Peru
reason: Peru has investor and rentista rows but no general_permanent_residence row. The three-year consecutive-residence rule is quoted from the gob.pe page and corroborated from the Reglamento PDF (art. 93.1). Authorable at high, with the 183-day absence rule and the S/ 55,000 gross annual income floor for conversion recorded.

finding_title: Calidad migratoria Investigación / Investigador residente (researcher)
name: Peru
reason: talent_skilled; no Peruvian row covers it. Distinct from the ordinary employer-sponsored trabajador permit because CONCYTEC gates it and the calidad authorises any income-generating activity rather than one employer. Quote verified on gob.pe, statutory wording corroborated from DL 1350 art. 29.2 lit. g via El Peruano.

finding_title: Calidad migratoria Nómada Digital (enacted 2023, not yet grantable)
name: Peru
reason: New row, but it MUST NOT be authored as active. The nomada digital calidad exists in law (DL 1582, in force 15 November 2023) and is quoted from El Peruano, but Migraciones' own press note says it will only be granted once the implementing resolucion is published and the TUPA procedure exists, and the trametes index still carries no entry for it. High confidence attaches to the finding that it is enacted and not operational. Because the row would not be active, it does not reduce the active-below-high count.

finding_title: Residente Pensionado (Ley 694 retiree residence)
name: Nicaragua
reason: The shipped row fuses pensionado and rentista under one min_income of USD 1,000, but Ley 694 as reformed by Ley 987 sets USD 1,000 for pensionado and USD 1,250 for rentista — two thresholds, two rows. This is the pensionado half. NOT high: the quote does not re-verify against the cited URL, because digesto.asamblea.gob.ni serves the statutory text by AJAX POST and a plain GET of source_url returns a JavaScript shell. Administrative availability is also unconfirmed (migob.gob.ni and asamblea.gob.ni both 403).

finding_title: Residente Rentista (Ley 694 passive-income residence)
name: Nicaragua
reason: Rentista half of the same split, at USD 1,250/month from foreign-generated income. Same blocker: not re-fetchable from source_url as cited. Worth applying regardless of confidence is the stale-figure correction — the widely repeated USD 600 pensionado / USD 750 rentista figures are pre-2019 and wrong.

finding_title: Investor / other residence categories under Ley 761, Ley General de Migración y Extranjería
name: Nicaragua
reason: cannot_determine. Only the TITLE of Ley 761 is vouched for character-for-character; no article text was pulled, so nothing can be said about whether it contains an investor residence category, and no figure may be inferred. Nicaragua has no investor residence row and this does not create one.
